image_description: A close-up portrait of a male Mallard duck (drake) floating on water. The subject features a characteristic iridescent green head, a distinct white neck ring, a yellow bill, and mottled brown/grey chest plumage. The background consists of rippling water with another out-of-focus duck visible in the upper left.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, and flat with a distinct yellow coloration consistent with a male Mallard.
The eye is visible and appears dark/black, matching the biological description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body shows dense, layered feather texture typical of waterproof plumage, and the posture suggests buoyancy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image perfectly matches the Mallard drake description: iridescent green head, clear white neck ring, and brownish-grey chest feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The duck is floating on water; legs and feet are submerged and completely occluded from view.
The wings are folded against the body and largely occluded by the angle and crop of the image; only the shoulder area is visible.
